summary: Plot 0 follows the roof-height map: a 141-high pale limestone slab (with a penthouse to y 148) stepping down 132/105/59 toward Fifth Avenue, and a six-storey U podium plus Fifth Ave wings with roof gardens on setback decks at y 26. A stepped Deco portal frames the open forecourt where bronze ATLAS kneels under a 9-ring copper armillary sphere, between granite pylons. Atlas's real spot is in the notch at x 72..83, which is off the footprint, so the forecourt is pushed back to x 63..71 where the map shows a low 17-18 block. The British Empire Building and La Maison Française are identical six-storey twins with deeper setback storeys, gardened roofs and gilded relief panels over their Fifth Ave doors. Continuous piers, dark window strips, ~25% lit windows and floodlit setback decks make it read as Rockefeller Center from the air at dusk.
